basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Non erit hic haeres tuus, sed qui egredietur de utero tuo, ipsum habebis haeredem. Quod'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Non erit hic haeres tuus, sed qui egredietur de utero tuo, ipsum habebis haeredem. Quod de Isaac et semine ejus dictum ratio probat; de quo postmodum audivit: Quia in Isaac vocabitur tibi semen. Neque enim filii concubinarum, etsi Abrahae semen sunt, haereditatis ejus participes esse potuerunt; et quoniam ad hanc haereditatem Deo dilectam in qua protectio divina, et merces esset magna futura, coelestes solum animae pertinent, apte subnectitur:
